name: scan-security-headers
description: Scans web applications, APIs, reverse proxies, CDN configuration, and middleware for missing or unsafe HTTP security headers, cookie flags, CORS policy, CSP, HSTS, clickjacking protections, MIME sniffing protections, referrer policy, and browser-facing misconfiguration.
instructions:
# scan-security-headers

Scans browser-facing HTTP response hardening controls.

## Orchestration

1. Load `references/rules.yaml` to get the active `SHD-` rule set.
2. Load `../_shared/owasp-cheatsheets.yaml` and use the mapped OWASP cheat sheets to support remediation guidance and references.
3. Identify target evidence from source code, configuration, tests, API specs, IaC, CI/CD, runtime manifests, and documentation relevant to the request.
4. Evaluate each rule using its `match_strategy`, preserving file path, line, snippet, control context, and confidence.
5. Mark each rule `Pass`, `Fail`, `Partial`, `Unknown`, or `Not Applicable` based on available evidence.
6. Prioritize findings by severity, exploitability, exposed surface, and whether a concrete remediation is available.
7. Render the final report using `references/report-template.md`.

## Usage

Scan the current repository:

```text
/scan-security-headers
```

Scan a specific path:

```text
/scan-security-headers src/ services/ docs/
```

## OWASP Cheat Sheets

Use the shared mapping in `../_shared/owasp-cheatsheets.yaml` for authoritative OWASP Cheat Sheet Series references that match this skill. Include the relevant cheat sheet links in the report when they directly support a finding or remediation.

## Review Guidance

Prioritize production routes, authenticated pages, admin surfaces, OAuth redirects, file downloads, and any response that handles sensitive data.

rules.name: Require Strict-Transport-Security
rules.description: Identify missing or weak HSTS on HTTPS applications.
rules.remediation: Set Strict-Transport-Security with adequate max-age, includeSubDomains where safe, and preload when appropriate.

rules.name: Require a restrictive Content-Security-Policy
rules.description: Identify missing or overly permissive CSP such as unsafe-inline or wildcard script sources.
rules.remediation: Deploy a restrictive CSP and remove unsafe script/style allowances where possible.

rules.name: Prevent framing
rules.description: Identify missing X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors for sensitive pages.
rules.remediation: Use CSP frame-ancestors and/or X-Frame-Options DENY/SAMEORIGIN.

rules.name: Disable content sniffing
rules.description: Identify missing X-Content-Type-Options on browser content.

rules.name: Limit referrer leakage
rules.remediation: Set strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter based on app needs.

rules.name: Require secure cookie attributes
rules.description: Identify session or sensitive cookies missing Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, or appropriate scope.
rules.remediation: Set Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, and narrow Domain/Path attributes.

rules.name: Detect permissive CORS
rules.description: Identify wildcard/reflected origins, broad methods, or credentials with permissive origins.
rules.remediation: Use explicit origin allowlists and avoid credentialed broad CORS.

rules.name: Restrict browser features
rules.description: Identify missing Permissions-Policy on sensitive apps.
rules.remediation: Disable unneeded browser capabilities such as camera, microphone, geolocation, and payment.

rules.name: Prevent sensitive response caching
rules.description: Identify sensitive authenticated responses without no-store/private caching directives.
rules.remediation: Set Cache-Control: no-store for sensitive responses.

rules.name: Avoid relying on X-XSS-Protection
rules.description: Identify reliance on deprecated X-XSS-Protection as primary XSS defense.
rules.remediation: Use CSP and output encoding; set X-XSS-Protection to 0 if needed to avoid browser quirks.

rules.name: Review cross-origin isolation headers
rules.description: Identify missing cross-origin isolation where SharedArrayBuffer or sensitive embedding protections are needed.
rules.remediation: Set COOP, COEP, and CORP according to application compatibility.

rules.name: Reduce server and framework disclosure
rules.description: Identify verbose Server, X-Powered-By, or framework headers.
rules.remediation: Remove or minimize technology disclosure headers.
